The furnaces under the plains burned for an age before the ash came down, and someone had to feed them. When the fire got loose, the Stoker stayed, and he never put his shovel down. Where the Emberwright burns the night back from afar, he walks into the thick of it: wide blows, thrown coals, and shouts that carry over the horde. Explosions only stoke him.
He has his own skills and his own gear to find: fireboxes, blades and charms. He's brand new, so expect his numbers to change as we see how he plays.

The game now uses the Neutral colour look by default: truer fire colours. You were on Filmic, the old default, and have been moved to Neutral. You can change it any time in Settings, under Display: Colour.

Act 2: Steamfen is coming
A drowned kiln city in a steaming marsh. The nagas hunt in the water, and their Abbess commands the flood.
Clearer fights, and fire on phones
Fire shows on phones again: Flame Wake's trail, flames, explosions, burning ground and the lava were missing.
On phones the night is brighter: the ground and the horde are easier to see, and the fire is as bright as before.

Clearer fights: a boss no longer drowns in your fire. A foe hit again and again shows fewer full blasts, and a boss shows through the fire on him. See Hit Effects under Gameplay in Settings to choose how much (100% is every hit in full, as before).
The colour look is Neutral by default now (it was Filmic): truer fire colours. If you liked it as it was, choose Filmic under Display: Colour in Settings.
The Quencher, and better fire
Late in the night a new foe walks with the horde: the Quencher. Its steam washes your marks off the foes around it, and for a few seconds none will take.
Burning ground looks like fire now: low flames on glowing cracks instead of a flat glowing disc. An enemy's fire marks where it stops hurting with a line of embers.
The Ash Plains have an end
Something waits at the end of the night, after the Pyre Hierophant. Bring it down and the dawn comes.
At the dawn, leave the plains with your score, or hold the line: night falls again and the run goes on, harder.
A sun by your name on the leaderboard once you've seen the dawn.
Easier Easy, and a Hearth that changes your runs
Easy is a good deal easier: the horde toughens more slowly, hits softer and comes thinner, and potions heal more. Medium is a little easier too.

Four new unlocks at the Hearth: Kindred Flame (+1 to every skill's count), Foresight (four boons to choose from), Hearthfire (stronger potions) and Phoenix's Favour (once a run, the Phoenix raises you from death).
The Mother of Ash fights harder once she's wounded.
The enemies' bigger fires show a red edge where the danger ends, and your own fire can burn gold or red instead (Settings: My Fire).
Settings in tabs: Gameplay, Display and Graphics.
Gear that combines your skills
13 new items that make your skills work together: fire hits harder on Shocked foes, a killed Branded foe sets off the Burning ones round it, and more.
Every item now has a third tier, and picking up a copy of an item you wear upgrades it.
Item cards show which skills an item works with.
A Gear tab in the codex (K): every item you've seen, its tiers and what it works with.
Icons over enemies show the marks your gear uses (Settings: Mark Icons).
A narrator for the run's big moments (Settings: Narrator).
Calmer fire light in big fights, and dimmer braziers.
The Ash Plains, rebuilt
The map has places now: shrines, ruins, graveyards, lava fields, a fallen idol, and a chasm at the edge of the world.
Fires light the ground, and a low haze glows round them.
Smoother: no more hitches at level-ups, and faster frames.
New setting: Anti-aliasing.
Returning players only download what changed.
